subject.title: Add an FxTwitter read transport for public lookups, threads, profiles, and search

question: Should Birdclaw core own and support an opt-in FxTwitter transport, including its third-party privacy disclosure, availability expectations, and long-term configuration contract?
rationale: The existing architecture can accommodate another source, but accepting an external public service as a supported core transport is a product and maintenance commitment that code inspection cannot decide.

options.title: Sponsor a bounded core adapter
options.body: Approve an explicit, read-only FxTwitter MVP limited to public lookup, conversation, profile/status, and search operations with a safe self-hosted endpoint option.

options.title: Defer external-service support
options.body: Keep core live transport support limited to `bird` and `xurl` until reliability, ownership, or demand more clearly justifies another maintained integration.

options.title: Prototype outside core first
options.body: Validate normalization and operational behavior in an experimental consumer before committing the transport and configuration contract to Birdclaw core.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a bounded core adapter
recommendation.body: Approve an explicit, read-only FxTwitter MVP limited to public lookup, conversation, profile/status, and search operations with a safe self-hosted endpoint option.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision changes the core transport boundary governed by the product vision and the architecture he introduced.
